name: session1

messages.content: I want to turn the HACC hydro emulator's baryonic suppression into an actual weak-lensing forecast bias, not just a P(k) ratio. Plan: (1) get the emulator's S(k)=P_hydro/P_grav at z=0 for the fiducial point AND the weakest-feedback point in its design (minimum AGN kinetic feedback), on its full k-grid; (2) also get S(k) at z=0.5 and z=1 for both points, since a DES/LSST-like lensing kernel integrates over z~0.3-1.5. Use list_observables, describe_parameters, and predict_observable. Report the parameter values for both points explicitly, and give me the S(k) arrays (or at least S at k=0.1,0.5,1,2,3,5,8 h/Mpc for each z) in a table. Do not round away the small deviations near k=0.1-0.5 h/Mpc; I need those to judge whether a large-scale-only lensing analysis could even see this.

I'll start by finding out which observables are available and what the parameter space covers.

I ran all six S(k) predictions, but I can't give you the table. None of my tools can read a CSV back, so I have not seen a single S(k) value. Every number is only in files on disk. Writing down values for k = 0.1 to 8 h/Mpc would mean making them up, and that is especially risky for the small deviations at k = 0.1 to 0.5 you need. One overlay plot (Figure 10) was made, but it is not a substitute for the numbers.

**The two points, at z = 0, 0.5 and 1**

The emulator doesn't define a "fiducial" point or a "weakest-feedback" point, and none of my tools list the 110 simulation parameter sets. So both points below are my own choices, not actual design runs.

| Parameter | Fiducial (centre of each range) | Minimum kinetic feedback |
|---|---|---|
| κ_w (AGN wind coupling) | 3.0 | 3.0 |
| e_w (AGN energy efficiency) | 0.6 | 0.6 |
| M_seed [10⁶ M_sun] | 1.3 | 1.3 |
| v_kin [10⁴ km/s] | 0.65 | **0.1** (range minimum) |
| ε_kin [units of 10¹] | 0.61 | **0.02** (range minimum) |
| ω_m = Ω_m h² | 0.1375 | 0.1375 |
| σ_8 | 0.8 | 0.8 |

Design ranges: κ_w 2–4, e_w 0.2–1.0, M_seed 0.6–2.0, v_kin 0.1–1.2, ε_kin 0.02–1.2, ω_m 0.12–0.155, σ_8 0.7–0.9. No calls returned extrapolation warnings.

Things to keep in mind:
- **The "weak" point is a corner of the design space.** Setting v_kin and ε_kin both to their minimum, with everything else at the centre, puts the point at the edge of the space. It is unlikely to sit next to any of the 110 Latin-hypercube runs. Treat the GP standard deviation (`y_std`) there with caution, and check it before trusting the near-1 values at low k.
- **"Weakest" here means only the AGN kinetic channel.** Lowering e_w or κ_w could reduce suppression further. I did not test that.
- **The k-grid has 799 bins in h/Mpc,** but the tool didn't report its limits. Check that 0.1 and 8 h/Mpc fall inside it.
- **The z = 0.5 and z = 1 outputs are real snapshots, not interpolated.** The emulator was trained at z = 0, 0.1, 0.5, 1 and 2. Your lensing kernel reaches z ≈ 1.5, which falls between the z = 1 and z = 2 snapshots, so S(k) there would be interpolated.

**Files** (columns: `x` = k in h/Mpc, `y_mean` = S(k), `y_std` = GP 1σ)

Base directory: `/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/expert-baryon-lensing-bias-2/runs/261024_185342/`
- Fiducial: `fiducial/Pk-ratio_z0.0000_prediction.csv`, `fiducial/Pk-ratio_z0.5000_prediction.csv`, `fiducial/Pk-ratio_z1.0000_prediction.csv`
- Minimum kinetic feedback: `weak_kin/Pk-ratio_z0.0000_prediction.csv`, `weak_kin/Pk-ratio_z0.5000_prediction.csv`, `weak_kin/Pk-ratio_z1.0000_prediction.csv`
- Figure 10 (`Pk-ratio_comparison.png`): all six curves, plotted as ratios to fiducial z = 0.

Warning: don't use the three `Pk-ratio_z*.csv` files in the base directory itself. My first batch wrote both points to the same file names, so each file holds whichever finished last. I reran everything into the subfolders above.

**Next steps**
1. To get the table, read off the values with a few lines of code: interpolate `y_mean` and `y_std` at k = 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8, and print to five or six decimals. Then compare |1 − S| with `y_std` at k ≤ 0.5. A deviation smaller than the emulator's own uncertainty can't be detected from this emulator, let alone from a large-scale-only lensing analysis.
2. If you can give me the actual parameter set of the least-suppressed simulation (for example from the design table in the emulator paper), I'll rerun at that point.
3. To get the lensing bias, weight the per-redshift S(k) by your survey's convergence power spectrum integral, at ℓ ≈ k·χ(z), and compare it with the gravity-only result (the emulator also provides a gravity-only spectrum, `Pk_GO`). I can generate the matching gravity-only spectra on the same grid if useful.
